The (<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mu \tau)_{e}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is about <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$5.21\times 10^{-4}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> cm2/V in CZT with more oxygen and <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$2.33\times 10^{-3}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> cm2/V with less oxygen. The mobility is obtained from the results of the time of flight (TOF) testing through the laser-beam-induced current (LBIC) technique, to be around 1000 cm2/V<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\cdot $ </tex-math></inline-formula>s1 for both samples, and the lifetime to be 494 and 2407 ns, respectively. It can be concluded that oxygen-related defects can terribly affect the electron transport properties.

articleTitle: Climate Reanalysis of Electron Radiation Belt Long-Term Dynamics Using a Dedicated Numerical Scheme
abstract: Climate reanalysis represents a valuable tool to improve radiation belt specification models such as ONERA’s global radiation Earth environment (GREEN) model. Generally, it consists in the elaboration of a long-term database of best estimates by the assimilation of in situ data in radiation belt theoretical models such as ONERA’s Salammbô code. However, their construction needs strong confidence in the code’s physical description, but also in its numerical resolution. We present in this article the new numerical solver of Salammbô. The latter provides stronger accuracy, robustness, and efficiency arguments that will ensure more reliable estimations from Salammbô. In addition, we will show how these improvements will open the path to the improvement of the GREEN model, through climate reanalysis.

articleTitle: Fusion Neutron-Induced Soft Errors During Long Pulse D–D Plasma Discharges in the WEST Tokamak
abstract: We have performed real-time soft error rate (RT-SER) measurements on bulk 65-nm static random access memories (SRAMs) during deuterium-deuterium (D-D) plasma operation at W-tungsten–Environment in Steady-state Tokamak (WEST). The present measurement campaign was characterized by the production of several tens of long pulse discharges (~60 s) and by a total neutron fluence (at the level of the circuits under test) up to <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\sim 10^{9}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> n<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\cdot $ </tex-math></inline-formula> cm-2, improving the error statistics by a factor of more than 6 with respect to the first measurements obtained in 2020. The experimental results demonstrate the occurrence of bursts of single-event upsets (SEUs) during the most efficient shots and 12% of multiple cell upset (MCU) events. Time-resolved data also show that MCUs are preferentially detected in the last part of these long pulses, providing further evidence that higher energy neutrons, initiated by deuterium-tritium (D-T) reactions due to triton burn-up in the D-D plasma, may play a role in the production of MCUs that cannot be attributed in such large proportions to “low-energy” neutrons produced in D-D reactions.

articleTitle: Electron Beam Dosimetry for Space Solar Cell Radiation Qualifications
abstract: The implications of common dosimetry methods used in electron beam irradiations for the space qualification of photovoltaics are described. The maximum power degradation of advanced solar cell technologies is compared as a function of electron fluence obtained from two electron irradiation facilities. The significant difference in the degradation rates between the two facilities suggests a systematic error in the electron fluence. The difference in dosimetry is examined using MCNP6.2 Monte Carlo simulations for ionizing and displacement damage dose (DDD) depositions along the electron beam path for each facility. It is shown that the 1-MeV electron beam flux, as determined from ionizing dosimetry methods, is overestimated by >24% compared to a nonionizing dosimetry counterpart. The error results from not properly accounting for the degradation of the electron beam energy and flux through the beam window and air gap.

articleTitle: A Wide-Tuning PLL With SET-Tolerant Quadrature Ring VCO for Serial Rapid I/O
abstract: This article presents a single-event transient (SET) tolerant phase-locked loops (PLLs) with a wide-tuning-range source-feedforward ring voltage-controlled oscillator (SFRVCO), suitable for serial rapid I/O (SRIO). The analysis of impulse sensitivity function (ISF) shows that the proposed oscillator has lower phase noise, and its tuning range reaches 0.9–6.6 GHz under the control of adjustable current source with high power supply rejection ratio (PSRR), which also exhibits better SET tolerance. Implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process, the proposed SFRVCO achieves a phase noise of −96.7 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset from a 2.5-GHz carrier, occupying a core area of 0.0008 mm2. Laser experiments indicate an irradiation threshold of 600 pJ.

articleTitle: Special NSREC 2023 Issue of the IEEE Transactions on Nuclear Science Editor Comments
abstract: The April 2024 Special Issue of the IEEE Transactions on Nuclear Science (TNS) contains selected papers from the 60th annual IEEE International Nuclear and Space Radiation Effects Conference (NSREC), which was held in Kansas City, MO, USA, from July 24 to 28, 2023. The IEEE NSREC is sponsored by the IEEE Nuclear and Plasma Sciences Society. More than 55 of the papers presented during NSREC are included in this year’s special issue. This issue is not a conference proceeding or a conference record. Papers that appear in this issue have all successfully completed the regular journal review process before the special issue deadline. A few other papers presented during the conference may appear in the subsequent issues of IEEE TNS.

articleTitle: Search for Editor-in-Chief
Comments by the Senior Editor
abstract: The 8th edition of the International Conference on “Advancements in Nuclear Instrumentation Measurement Methods and their Applications” (ANIMMA) was held in Lucca, Italy, on June 12–16, 2023. The ANIMMA-2023 welcomed 403 attendees from 31 nationalities, including 81 graduated students coming from academy, research institutes, and industry to discuss new scientific and technical prospects in all fields, where nuclear instrumentation and measurement techniques play a major role.

articleTitle: Comments by the Editors
abstract: The August 2024 special issue of the IEEE Transactions on Nuclear Science (TNS) contains more than 60 peer-reviewed journal articles prepared on the basis of presentations made at the 2023 Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS), held in Toulouse, France, September 25–29, 2023. Additional papers presented at RADECS 2023 are available in the conference proceedings, available through IEEE Xplore.

articleTitle: Corrections to “Multilayer Perception Model Versus Charge Comparison Method for Neutron/Gamma Discrimination in Plastic Scintillator According to Sampling Frequency and Energy Radiation” [Sep 23 2212-2217]
abstract: The code used to prepare the dataset in the above article <xref ref-type="bibr" rid="ref1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</xref> contained a minor error. articleTitle: Introducing a New Associate Editor for Accelerator Technology
abstract: IEEE Transactions on Nuclear Science (TNS) is pleased to announce that Dr. Jiaru Shi has accepted an appointment as an Associate Editor handling papers on accelerator technology. He will be working alongside Dr. Evegenya Simakov, who will be continuing in her role as an Associate Editor.

Editorial Conference Summary by the General Chair
abstract: The 60th IEEE Nuclear and Space Radiation Effects Conference (NSREC) was held on July 24–28, 2023, at the Sheraton Kansas City Hotel at Crown Center, Kansas City, MO, USA. The 60th NSREC celebrated with special pins for the attendees and special cake and cupcakes on Thursday. The 2023 NSREC was attended by 534 engineers, scientists, managers, students, and exhibitors. International participation was also strong, with 88 non-U.S. attendees from Belgium, Canada, China, Czech Republic, Finland, France, Germany, India, Israel, Italy, Japan, Korea, Netherlands, Poland, Sweden, Switzerland, and U.K.

articleTitle: IEEE Transactions on Nuclear Science 2024 Best Paper Award
abstract: The IEEE Transactions on Nuclear Science Best Paper Award is an annual award recognizing the most significant paper published in the TRANSACTIONS in a given year. The award is sponsored by the IEEE Nuclear and Plasma Sciences Society and the winning paper is selected according to its quantifiable usefulness to the community. The authors of papers published in the TRANSACTIONS in the third year prior to the year of the award are eligible for consideration. Thus, the 2024 award is awarded to the paper published in calendar year 2021 judged to be the most useful to our community based on metrics calculated for the years 2021, 2022, and 2023.

articleTitle: Outstanding Conference Paper Award: 2023 IEEE Nuclear and Space Radiation Effects Conference
abstract: The recipients of the 2023 NSREC Outstanding Conference Paper Award are Ali Jouni, Victor Malherbe, Bastien Mamdy, Thomas Thery, Vincent Correas, Serge De Paoli, Valérian Lalucaa, Cédric Virmontois, Gilles Gasiot, and Vincent Goiffon for their paper titled “Effect of Proton Energy and Bias Conditions During Irradiation on CMOS Single-Photon Avalanche Diodes.”
